doc.title: Eddie Marshall interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Race among musicians and record companies
summary: He says race is always an issue in America, discusses record company preferences, and says he likes playing with anybody.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Yeah. Has the scene between musicians and — has the racial scene between musicians changed over the years? Or was it ever an issue at all?

Oh it’s always an issue. This is America. It’s always an issue. It’s either white musicians feel that the record companies are slamming them because they just want to record black musicians — that was a thing a few years ago. And it was probably true too for the record companies. I mean I don’t know if I want to even go there. I mean because it’s like they use that thing where they’re pushing young musicians and then pushing all black musicians — you know wherever the money flow goes, that’s where the record companies go. Not to say that there’s not a lot of good music being recorded. But a lot of it — but the racial thing, you know it’s probably least — you know we’re musicians, jazz musicians, I think we’re probably wise enough now to know that neither of us are making any money. You know what I’m saying? Like I don’t even see where that ever comes in. I mean it’s like some people will ask me “oh is it better playing — do you like playing with white musicians better than you like playing with black musicians?” I mean you always get that. And it’s like, I like playing with anybody. Now if somebody can’t play, that’s a different thing. You don’t have to be black or white and be sad. I mean if you think of a thing of comfort now, now sometimes either you might think yeah, he sounds good, he’s playing with all these black musicians. But those guys are probably all my old buddies that I’ve known forever and we have this comarad — there always is going to be this thing about, like if all Jewish people get together and you know you’re in this family, you’re having a ball, because you’re enjoying each other, you’re enjoying each other’s Jewishness or whatever it is.
Right. It’s not just a musical issue.
